title: A University Open Day
description: Four recordings from a university open day: a welcome talk, a chat about accommodation, a campus tour and an announcement.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · The welcome talk
parts.intro: You will hear a university professor welcoming visitors to the open day.

script.speaker: Dr Evans
script.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our open day. My name is Dr Evans, and I'm the head of student services. It's wonderful to see so many families here today.

script.speaker: Dr Evans
script.text: Let me explain the plan for the day. The talks about courses begin at ten o'clock in the main hall. They were going to start at half past nine, but we've changed the time because of the traffic.

script.speaker: Dr Evans
script.text: After the talks, you can take a tour of the campus. Tours leave from the front entrance every thirty minutes, and each one lasts about forty-five minutes.

script.speaker: Dr Evans
script.text: Lunch is free for all visitors in the student café. I recommend the vegetable pie, but if you prefer something lighter, there are also salads and fruit.

script.speaker: Dr Evans
script.text: This afternoon, our students will answer your questions in the library. Please remember that they are not teachers, so they can only talk about their own experience.

script.speaker: Dr Evans
script.text: A final piece of advice. Many visitors try to see everything, and then they feel tired and confused. Choose two or three things you really want to see, and enjoy them properly.

script.speaker: Dr Evans
script.text: Now, if you're interested in science courses, please follow the green signs. For arts and languages, follow the blue signs. Have a lovely day.

parts.title: Part 2 · Asking about accommodation
parts.intro: You will hear a visitor, Minh, asking a student guide, Lucy, about living at the university.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Excuse me, are you one of the student guides? I'd like to ask about accommodation.

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: Yes, of course. I'm in my second year, so I know it well. Are you thinking of living on campus?

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: I'm not sure. My family lives about fifty kilometres away, so travelling every day would be difficult.

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: Then I'd advise living on campus in the first year. It's a good way to make friends. The rooms are small, but they're warm and clean.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: How much does a room cost?

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: A single room is about one hundred and twenty pounds a week. A shared room is cheaper, around ninety pounds, but some people don't like sharing.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: I think I'd prefer my own room. Is there a kitchen?

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: Yes, one kitchen for every six rooms. It can get messy, to be honest, but you soon learn who the tidy people are.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: And what about the internet? I'll need it for my studies.

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: It's free and fast in all rooms. The only problem is on Sunday evenings, when everybody is online at the same time.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Thanks, Lucy. That's really helpful. How do I apply?

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: You fill in a form online after you receive your offer. But apply early, because the popular rooms go quickly.

parts.title: Part 3 · The campus tour
parts.intro: You will hear a student guide, Tom, giving a tour of the campus.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Hello, everyone. I'm Tom, and I study engineering. I'll show you the most important places on the campus. Please stay together, and ask questions at any time.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: On your left is the library. It's open until midnight during exam time, and there are quiet rooms on the second floor. If you want to talk with friends, use the ground floor.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Straight ahead is the sports centre. It has a swimming pool, a gym and tennis courts. Students get a membership for only ten pounds a month, which is much cheaper than a town gym.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Now we're walking past the science building. The laboratories are new, but the building itself is very old. In winter it's freezing, so my advice is to wear a warm jumper.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: The red building next to the lake is the students' union. There you can join clubs, from chess to mountain climbing. I joined the climbing club in my first week, and it changed my university life.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Finally, the bus stop. Buses to the city centre leave every ten minutes, and a student ticket is half the normal price. That's the end of the tour. Thank you for listening.

parts.title: Part 4 · An announcement
parts.intro: You will hear an announcement over the loudspeaker at the open day.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. This is an announcement for all visitors at the open day.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Because of the rain, the music concert on the lawn will now be held in the main hall at three o'clock instead of two.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: The last campus tour will leave the front entrance at half past three, not at four as it says in your programme.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: If you'd like to apply for a scholarship, please visit the information desk in the library before four o'clock. Staff will give you a leaflet and explain the rules.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: A blue car, parked near the sports centre, has its lights on. Would the owner please return to the car park?

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Finally, we would like to thank all of you for coming. Free bags with a university notebook are available as you leave. Thank you.
